text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Eaton's targets 31 stores: Thousands of jobs in peril as retailer plans to close or sell even high-profile outlets.
- Lap dancing an indecent act, top court rules: Verdict puts onus on police to enforce ban on erotic contact in Canadian bars.
- Somalia cover-up hastily spun, MD says: Murder diagnosis suppressed, inquiry told.
- Police must obey Charter in investigations abroad.
- Comet burning bright: Hale-Bopp puts on best show in years.
- Hong Kong treasury awash in cash: Tsang's days as budget chief may be ending, but he leaves colony in good shape.
- Magna cuts key German deals: Big first-half profit spurs auto parts giant to expand in European vehicle interiors market.
- The musical crapshoot: Companies usually lose money on new recording artists. The profit comes when sales reach platinum.
- Malls could lose half of stores on Eaton's list: Retailer hints number could grow.
- 'Uh-oh,' Silver Tusk issues new assay data: VSE firm shows much less gold, silver.
- Teleglobe goes head to head with U.S. giant.
- 32 Eaton's stores in firing line: In first blueprint for restructuring, the troubled retailer breaks bad news to employees across the country. Now begin the negotiations with landlords.
